name: secp256k1_discrete_log_retrieval

phase_0.boundary_condition: Input: secp256k1 public key point P = n×G. Output: private key scalar n such that n×G = P. Precondition: P is a valid point on secp256k1. Postcondition: private key n recovered via Pollard rho collision or Shor period-finding.

VINIT.justification: The scalar field F_q before any search begins — the void from which the private key emerges

TANCH.justification: The secp256k1 curve order q and prime field F_p that bound all valid keys — the terminal boundary of the search space

AFWD.justification: Forward walk n×G — advancing along the elliptic curve by repeated point addition

AREV.justification: Reverse walk — attempting the inverse operation to recover n from P, the hard direction that defines ECDLP

CLINK.justification: Composing successive point additions to build the distinguished-point trail — the crystal-link of the search

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: curve equation y squared equals x cubed plus 7
IMSCRIB.justification: The curve equation is self-referential — it defines the geometric substrate on which all key operations imscribe themselves

FSPLIT.justification: Pollard's rho splits the search into two pseudo-random walks — tortoise (slow) and hare (fast) — branching the state space

FFUSE.justification: When tortoise and hare walks collide at a distinguished point, the discrete log is recovered — the fuse that reconstitutes the private key

EVALT.justification: The tortoise walk succeeds — a valid n is found such that n×G equals the target public key P

EVALF.justification: The hare walk reaches a dead end or invalid candidate — this branch of the search is exhausted

ENGAGR.justification: Shor's period-finding holds success and failure simultaneously — the dialetheic B-state where all candidate keys coexist until measurement

IFIX.justification: The recovered private key is permanently fixed — irreversible record, cannot be undone

phase_2.split_element: FSPLIT partitions the search space into tortoise walk and hare walk
phase_2.split_input: search_space = public_point_P with unknown discrete log n
split_outputs: tortoise walk — slow pseudo-random point sequence
hare walk — fast pseudo-random point sequence
phase_2.fuse_element: FFUSE collision detection — when tortoise and hare walks intersect at a distinguished point, the discrete log is computed from the collision
phase_2.fuse_result: search_space = public_point_P with unknown discrete log n

phase_3.void_description: 00 — no key material — the scalar field before any search begins
phase_3.true_description: 01 — private key n found such that n times G equals the target public key
phase_3.false_description: 10 — search path exhausted or candidate n invalid — discrete log not found on this branch
phase_3.both_description: 11 — quantum superposition of all candidate keys — Shor period-finding holds success and failure simultaneously until measurement

steps.domain_action: initialize the scalar field search — the void before any key material exists
establish curve parameters — secp256k1 order q and prime field F_p bound the search space
invoke the curve equation y squared equals x cubed plus 7 — the geometric substrate self-imscribes
reference the forward walk — begin scalar multiplication along the curve
partition the search into tortoise (slow) and hare (fast) pseudo-random walks
compose point addition chain — crystal-link the distinguished-point trail
attempt the reverse walk — discrete log inversion, the hard direction
tortoise walk reaches a distinguished point — candidate private key found
hare walk reaches dead end — candidate rejected, branch exhausted
quantum branch — Shor superposition holds all candidates simultaneously in B-state
collision detection — tortoise and hare walks intersect, discrete log recovered from collision
write recovered private key to cold storage — irreversible fixation
close the system — key pair is sealed, retrieval complete

phase_5.compiler_frontend: ECDLP solver implementation — Pollard rho with distinguished points, baby-step giant-step, or Shor algorithm
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Elliptic curve point addition and scalar multiplication over the prime field F_p of secp256k1
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Distinguished-points hash table for collision detection across parallel walks
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Parallel walk coordinator distributing iterations across cores or quantum branches
phase_5.alfs_store: SEC 2 Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters — secp256k1 curve specification

phase_6.cycle_cost: Classical search irreversibly dissipates energy per Landauer principle — each iteration costs kT ln 2; quantum branch conserves entropy until measurement collapses the superposition
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Scalar field uninitialized — public key point P known but private key n unknown — maximum uncertainty
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Private key n recovered — entropy collapsed to a single known value — the key pair is determined
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: Delta S greater than zero for classical search — irreversible dissipation; Delta S approximately zero for quantum branch until measurement
